summary: James A. Santucci works in religious studies and Indology. He served as Professor of Religion at California State University (attested 1998) and as Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 2007).

James Adam (1860–1907) was a scholar in philosophy and other fields. He completed his education at the University of Aberdeen from circa 1876 to 1880 and at Gonville and Caius College from circa 1880 to 1884.

James Alan Matisoff is a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. Educated at Harvard, International Christian University, and UC Berkeley, he taught at Columbia University (1966–1969) and served as professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley from 1970 to 2002.

James Atkinson (1780–1852) was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He held posts at the India Government Mint in Kolkata (1812, 1818) and Fort William College (1818).

James B. Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his graduate and PhD studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in the 1990s, where he studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, John D. Dunne, and numerous other instructors.

James Blumenthal (1967–2014) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and held appointments at Oregon State University and Maitripa College (attested 2013–2015).

James Burgess (1832–1916) worked in archaeology and Indology after studying at Glasgow and Edinburgh. He served as Secretary of the Bombay Geographical Society and held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, including Director General from 1886 to 1889.

James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa (attested 1996).

James C. Dobbins specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. After earning his PhD from Yale University by 1984, he served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015–2019).

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland (1792–1844) was an Indologist. He studied at East India Company College, Fort William College, and under Thomas Roebuck, later serving as professor of law at Presidency University.

James Darmesteter (1849–1894) specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal, later holding posts there (~1877–1894) and at the Collège de France (1885–1894).

James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1964 to 1968 under Sheldon Pollock, and joined the faculty at the University of Iowa in 1971.
James Dwight Dana (1813–1895) studied at Yale College from circa 1830 to 1833. He later held an academic post at Yale University from circa 1850 to 1892, where he taught Charles Rockwell Lanman.
James Fergusson (1808–1886) studied at the Royal High School, Edinburgh. He held a post as a member of the Royal Asiatic Society beginning in 1840.

James Fieser is a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He completed his education at Berea College (~1976–1980) and Purdue University (~1981–1986), and held posts at the University of Tennessee and its Martin campus around 1992.

James G. Mullens is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Simon Fraser University, the University of Victoria, and McMaster University (PhD 1994) under Graeme MacQueen, and took a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James Gibbs (1825–1886) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai from 1870 to 1879 and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai from circa 1870 to 1881.

James H. Austin is a neurologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nanrei Sohaku Kobori and others. He held long-term posts at the University of Oregon (~1961–1965) and the University of Colorado (~1965–1992).

James Hadley (1821–1872) was a linguist and Indologist. After studying at Fairfield Academy, Yale College, and under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, he tutored at Middlebury College (1845) and served as Professor of Greek at Yale University (1845–1872).

James Haughton Woods (1864–1935) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religion. He studied at Harvard, the University of Strasbourg, and under Paul Deussen and Charles Rockwell Lanman, becoming a professor at Harvard University in 1914.
